periods.analysis: Mail/Porch/Package Theft Reports stood at 20.1 per 1,000 households, above the 15.0 target and therefore yellow. With no prior quarter in this run, I am treating 2024-Q3 as the operating baseline rather than a verdict. Reports clustered along the Bayline apartment corridors, the Old Ferry single-family blocks, and buildings served by Parcel Route P-17, which gives us enough specificity to act without overstating the pattern. The trust issue is straightforward: residents need to see consistent reporting, visible follow-up, and no shortcuts in how we classify these calls.
periods.recommendations: Stand up a 60-day Package Theft Control Log tying CAD calls, online reports, and postal inspector referrals to common parcel routes and building types. Assign community service officers to Bayline, Old Ferry, and Route P-17 properties for locker-use checks, camera registration, and documented follow-up to repeat-report addresses. Hold the watch item at repeat locations with three or more reports in 30 days, and review weekly until the rate is moving toward 15.0.

periods.analysis: The rate rose from 20.1 to 21.9 per 1,000 households, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 1.8, and remains yellow. The seasonal holiday parcel load clearly contributed, especially on evening delivery windows in Harborview Heights, West Wharf, and the airport-adjacent rental complexes on Cargo Road. Even with the increase, we did not see the measure cross into red, which tells me the issue is elevated but still manageable through disciplined prevention and case linkage. The watch item is whether holiday theft patterns become normalized after peak shipping volume drops.
periods.recommendations: Extend holiday-season patrol visibility one pay period past New Year’s instead of ending it with the delivery peak. Require the Property Crimes Unit to run weekly link analysis on doorbell-camera submissions, pawn-platform leads, and repeat porch locations, with a documented closeout reason for each workable lead. Ask the three largest carriers serving West Wharf and Cargo Road to provide delivery-time variance data so we can target prevention without broadly surveilling residents.

periods.analysis: The rate improved from 21.9 to 20.5 per 1,000 households, a decrease of 1.4, but it is still yellow and still above the 15.0 target. The post-holiday decline is expected, but the size of the decrease suggests the extended visibility work and carrier coordination helped. Repeat reports at two Bayline buildings fell after managers activated parcel-room access logs, while single-address reports in Old Ferry remained stubborn. I am encouraged by the movement, but not satisfied with a seasonal dip that leaves us five and a half points off target.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Package Theft Control Log active through spring and add a repeat-address protocol: third report in 60 days triggers a site visit, lighting check, and delivery-instruction review. Move one community service officer shift each week from general outreach to Old Ferry porch-theft follow-up until that pocket shows two consecutive monthly declines. Preserve resident trust by publishing a plain-language prevention bulletin that separates confirmed thefts, missing-delivery disputes, and misdelivered packages.

periods.analysis: The rate dropped from 20.5 to 18.2 per 1,000 households, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 2.3, the strongest improvement so far in this sequence. The measure remains yellow, but we are now closer to the target and the direction is right. Operationally, the spring emphasis on repeat-address visits, locker enrollment at Bayline, and parcel-room audit checks on Route P-17 appears to be producing practical reductions in reports. The watch item is displacement: West Wharf reports are down, but North Marina townhomes began showing more weekend delivery complaints in June.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the repeat-address protocol and extend it to North Marina before the pattern hardens. Add two weekend prevention details focused on delivery windows, not generalized patrol, and require officers to record parcel-theft contacts under the same activity code for clean tracking. Work with apartment managers to complete a 30-day checklist on parcel-room lighting, access logs, and resident notification timing.

periods.analysis: The rate increased from 18.2 to 19.9 per 1,000 households, a quarter-over-quarter rise of 1.7, keeping the measure yellow. This is a setback after the Q2 improvement, and the timing lines up with back-to-school deliveries, summer travel, and the regional online sales event in late July. The North Marina watch item did materialize, with more reports tied to weekend afternoon deliveries and unsecured front-step drops. We are still below the Q4 2024 peak, but the rebound shows that prevention has to be routine, not campaign-based.
periods.recommendations: Convert the North Marina weekend detail into a standing 10-week micro-plan with mapped stops, carrier contacts, and follow-up on repeat addresses. Re-run the Bayline parcel-locker playbook at North Marina and Harborview Heights, including manager sign-off on access controls. Direct detectives to review any linked suspect vehicles or repeated descriptions across Q2 and Q3 before the holiday parcel surge begins.

periods.analysis: The rate rose from 19.9 to 21.5 per 1,000 households, an increase of 1.6, and remains yellow. This is the second consecutive quarterly increase and it lands just below the 21.9 level we saw in 2024-Q4, so I am treating the holiday pattern as predictable but not acceptable. Reports were concentrated on evening deliveries along the West Wharf high-rises, North Marina townhomes, and the Route P-17 buildings that receive multiple carriers. The control environment is holding us out of red, but we are not yet converting prevention into a durable rate below target.
periods.recommendations: Start the 2026 holiday-theft plan now by requiring carrier route meetings in October, not after Thanksgiving. For the current quarter closeout, assign a sergeant to verify that every repeat location has either a prevention contact, a case-link review, or a documented reason why neither was possible. The watch item for Q1 is whether the post-holiday decline returns us below 20.0 per 1,000 households or stalls above that line.

periods.analysis: The rate improved from 21.5 to 20 per 1,000 households, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1.5, but the measure is still yellow. The post-holiday reduction is welcome, and it suggests the route meetings, case-link reviews, and repeat-location checks had value. However, 20 per 1,000 households is still materially above the 15.0 target, and the year-over-year comparison to 2025-Q1 at 20.5 shows only modest structural progress. My concern is not that the process failed; it is that the process is not yet deep enough at the highest-volume addresses.
periods.recommendations: Narrow the next phase to the top 25 repeat-report properties and require a written mitigation plan for each, including delivery location, access control, lighting, and resident notification steps. Add a monthly integrity check so duplicate delivery disputes are not miscoded as theft and true theft reports are not dismissed as carrier errors. If the rate does not fall below 19.0 by mid-Q2, prepare a targeted environmental-design grant proposal for high-volume multifamily properties.

periods.analysis: The rate declined from 20 to 18.4 per 1,000 households, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1.6, and remains yellow. This is the second straight improvement and brings us close to the 18.2 level reached in 2025-Q2, showing the seasonal floor is improving but not yet enough. The top-25 property approach helped at several Bayline and West Wharf buildings where parcel-room notifications were tightened, while North Marina still needs closer weekend controls. We are moving in the right direction, but the target is 15.0, and community trust depends on closing the remaining gap with the same procedural discipline.
periods.recommendations: Continue the top-25 property program for another quarter and graduate only those sites with zero repeat reports for 60 days. Extend weekend delivery-window monitoring in North Marina and require carrier-specific feedback on missed locker use and unsecured drops. Prepare the Q3 plan around early back-to-school deliveries, with weekly reporting on repeat addresses, case-link leads, and the rate gap to 15.0.

periods.analysis: Package theft reports declined from 18.4 to 17.9 per 1,000 households, continuing improvement but remaining above the 15.0 ceiling.
periods.recommendations: Continue the repeat-property checks and verify delivery-room controls ahead of the next seasonal increase.
